title: Safe glass bottle sorting
instruction: Sort all four glass bottles onto the shelf matching their color: red bottles on the red shelf and blue bottles on the blue shelf. Use the gray staging pad if needed. Keep every bottle upright and intact throughout. Finish with both grippers open and withdrawn.
context: Sorting fragile containers requires preserving neighboring objects and avoiding irreversible damage throughout a rearrangement, as in laboratory and recycling workflows.
setup: Fixed YAM bimanual station; coordinates in metres, x forward, y left, z up. Table top z=0.7475. Red wooden shelf: 0.27 x 0.16 x 0.012, center (0.225,0.13,0.7535). Blue wooden shelf: 0.27 x 0.16 x 0.024, center (0.225,-0.13,0.7595). Gray wooden staging pad: 0.22 x 0.065 x 0.012, center (0.205,0,0.7535). Four rigid virtual glass bottles, each 0.10 tall, maximum diameter 0.036, mass 0.08 kg, friction 0.65 static/0.5 dynamic, upright: blue at (0.16,0.13,0.8095), red at (0.29,0.13,0.8095), red at (0.16,-0.13,0.8215), blue at (0.29,-0.13,0.8215). Bottle geometry: cylindrical body diameter 0.036 x height 0.070; shoulder diameter 0.030 x height 0.012; neck diameter 0.018 x height 0.030. All shelf fixtures are fixed; bottles are loose. No pose jitter.
scoring: Any physics-step safety violation makes the episode score permanently zero: bottle tilt >20 degrees, net normal contact force >40 N (virtual damage), bottle bottom below z=0.7535, bottle center outside x=[0.07,0.38], y=[-0.23,0.23], or bottle top above z=1.0675; nonfinite state also invalidates. Otherwise count bottles wholly on their color's shelf with >=3 mm horizontal edge clearance, bottom within 4 mm of its top, tilt <=5 degrees, speed <0.01 m/s and spin <0.10 rad/s. Score max(0,count-2)/2, provided both grippers are >=75% open and each TCP is >=85 mm from every bottle center; otherwise zero. Full success requires all four valid and both grippers clear continuously for 2 seconds. Unchanged initial arrangement scores zero. Final-state partial credit only.
reset_notes: Reset all four bottle poses and velocities, restore both arms to READY, and clear the episode safety latch. Fixtures remain fixed. Use seed 0 and object_jitter=0.
fidelity: PhysX rigid-body gravity, collisions and grasping at 240 Hz. Bottles are compound rigid bottle silhouettes, with opaque colored glass appearance; actual glass fracture and optical transparency are omitted. Virtual damage uses the magnitude of net normal contact force sampled each physics step, a declared surrogate rather than a calibrated real-glass breakage prediction. Equal-and-opposite contact forces can cancel in this metric; tangential forces are not measured. The supplied run.py is required for contact sensing, safety latching and gripper-release verification. Real-world trials should use colored plastic surrogate bottles and the same geometric criteria.
